FINDING_ID: Codex_R7_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.84  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector` and `DiminishingReturnsDetector` treat missing or future `round_idx` values as if they were legitimate late rounds, and both can emit false stop signals. `ConvergenceDetector.converged(r)` will happily compute on a round that was never recorded, because missing rounds default to empty findings and empty novelty, which can yield `kappa=1.0`. `DiminishingReturnsDetector.stop(r)` can also return `True` for an unrecorded future round because `smoothed_marginal_value()` falls back to `0.0` on an empty window. I reproduced `converged(5) == True` after recording only round 0, and `stop(5) == True` after recording only rounds 0-1. A simple off-by-one or stale round index can therefore fabricate termination.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Reject unknown round indices in all metric APIs, or require explicit contiguous registration before any convergence/stop computation.

FINDING_ID: Codex_R7_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.73  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager` continues to offer scheduling decisions after the FSM is terminal. `get_allocation()` checks only whether any active models remain; it does not check `self.fsm.is_terminal`. I reproduced `FAIL_CRITICAL -> TERMINAL` and then a successful `get_allocation()` returning a live allocation anyway. That means a caller can keep dispatching work after abort, convergence, or max-round termination, which breaks the manager’s own stop boundary.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make `get_allocation()` and `check_dispatch_feasibility()` raise once the FSM is terminal, unless an explicit override is requested.

FINDING_ID: Codex_R7_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.80  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector` caches equivalence classes by round index only, but the clustering semantics depend on mutable configuration (`tau_sim`) and possibly a replaceable `similarity_fn`. If either changes mid-run, cached classes are silently reused under the old threshold. I reproduced this by building round-0 classes with `tau_sim=0.9`, then lowering `tau_sim` to `0.8`; `get_round_classes(0)` still returned the old two-class result instead of re-clustering to one class. This makes adaptive threshold tuning unsafe and can desynchronise analytics from the config the user thinks is active.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Freeze similarity-related config after detector construction, or invalidate/rebuild caches whenever similarity semantics change.

FINDING_ID: Codex_R7_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.75  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.88  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: Several public config knobs are inert. `blind_first`, `theta_col`, `delta_deg`, and `default_vulnerability` are exposed as tunable parameters but are never actually consulted by the implementation. I verified `DynamicManagementConfig(blind_first=False)` still starts in `BLIND`, and `default_vulnerability=0.75` has no effect because unknown model pairs still return `0.0` vulnerability. `theta_col` and `delta_deg` appear only at their definitions. This makes the configuration surface non-authoritative: users can “set” behavior that the system never honors.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either wire these fields into runtime behavior or remove them and fail fast on unsupported configuration.

FINDING_ID: Codex_R7_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.77  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: The monitoring protocol cannot represent most of the recovery policy. `RecoveryAction` includes `RETRY_EXTENDED`, `RETRY_CLARIFIED`, `DEGRADE`, `DOWNGRADE_ROLE`, and `LOG_ONLY`, but `ManagerEventType` has no corresponding event types. This is deeper than “recovery events are not emitted”: even if emission were added, the PM-facing event taxonomy still cannot faithfully encode several real recovery outcomes. Any future integration would have to collapse distinct actions into lossy placeholders or omit them.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Align `ManagerEventType` with `RecoveryAction`, or emit a generic recovery event carrying the precise action in metadata.
